page: Microsoft Azure E48as_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on AMD EPYC 9V45 processors operating at up to 4.5 GHz. Allocated via Microsoft Hyper-V on an x86_64 architecture, the instance provides 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 24 physical cores with two threads per core. Memory capacity totals 384.0 GB of RAM, adhering strictly to an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio. The underlying AMD processor includes a hardware cache layout of 48 KB L1 data, 1.0 MB L2, and 32 MB L3 cache, alongside instruction set support for AVX-512 extensions including AVX-512 VNNI and BF16, as well as hardware cryptographic acceleration via AES and VAES. The configuration contains no dedicated GPUs and does not bundle local disk storage, relying entirely on remote managed disks.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong compute and in-memory execution profiles across multiple subsystems. Single-core stress-ng throughput places in the top 10% with a score of 3780.68, mirrored by high-tier single-threaded gzip compression at 41.17 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 18.13 GB/sec. Multi-threaded evaluations show consistent top-quartile execution, with a PassMark CPU score of 77976.45 and stress-ng multi-core output reaching 89464.17. Memory subsystems maintain high throughput, delivering 5014.67 GB/sec for small-block cached read operations and 102.69 GB/sec for large-block writes, though large-block uncached read operations fall into the average range at 153.62 GB/sec.

Data serving and inference workloads benefit from the dense memory-to-core allocation and vector-accelerated compute. Redis throughput yields 75.88 million SET operations per second, while static web serving achieves 61.28 GB/sec. On CPU-driven language model inference, the instance achieves top-tier results for small 135M parameter models, sustaining 4332.45 tokens per second in prompt processing and 428.63 tokens per second during generation. For medium 7B parameter models, prompt evaluation processes at 153.89 tokens per second while generation delivers 37.03 tokens per second.

Cost efficiency is driven by the 1:8 core-to-memory density, offering an effective compute and memory balance for systems that exceed standard memory thresholds without necessitating multi-socket bare-metal allocations. A structural tradeoff to consider is the absence of local ephemeral storage, which requires all disk I/O to be provisioned through remote network-attached volumes. This architecture fits in-memory caching platforms such as Redis, enterprise relational databases, big data analytics frameworks, and CPU-based lightweight AI inference.
description: Microsoft Azure E48as_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine equipped with 48 dedicated vCPUs and 384.0 GB of RAM, powered by AMD EPYC 9V45 processors running at 4.5 GHz on an x86_64 architecture. The system features 24 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading, advanced instruction support including AVX-512 VNNI and BF16, and no integrated local storage or GPU hardware. Performance testing highlights top-tier single-core compute and compression capabilities, alongside strong multi-core metrics, marked by a PassMark CPU score of 77976.45 and Redis throughput of 75.88 million operations per second. Memory bandwidth is robust for cached reads at 5014.67 GB/sec and write blocks at 102.69 GB/sec. Given its high memory ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU and lack of local disks, the E48as_v7 is tailored for in-memory databases, large-scale caching engines, relational database deployments, and CPU-driven machine learning inference.
